answer: Submissions that land within 136 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The glacier detector writes to vertex, and whisper reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 110 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 13 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
